headline: Ethiopia's Citizens Plant Their Way to Forest Recovery
meta_description: Ethiopia's Green Legacy Initiative has reversed a century of forest loss, with citizens planting billions of trees and shifting the nation's relationship with…
summary_short: Ethiopia reversed a century of deforestation by mobilizing citizens to plant trees. Forest cover rose from 15.5% to 23.6% in just a decade.
body:
Ethiopia spent most of the past century losing its forests—560,000 hectares stripped away for agriculture, logging, and charcoal fuel. In 2019, the government launched the Green Legacy Initiative, and something shifted. Citizens began planting. The official count stands at 48 billion trees in seven years, with a goal of 50 billion by 2030. While independent researchers question exact survival rates—some studies suggest nearly half of reforestation trees don't survive five years—the measurable outcome is undeniable: Ethiopia's deforestation rate plummeted from 92,000 hectares annually in 2013 to 27,703 hectares in 2023, a 70 percent drop. Forest cover rose from 15.5 to 23.6 percent over the same period.

But the real story lives in communities like Berbere, where Halima Kedir proved her skeptical neighbors wrong. She walks an hour each way to fetch water for her seedlings, treating each tree like an adopted child in the Oromo tradition. Thousands of households have followed. WaterAid Ethiopia distributed 55,000 indigenous seedlings across Berbere alone, with an 85 percent growth rate. Even Kedir's doubting neighbor Fate Abdulahi now calls her "a role model."

The initiative has united communities, universities, and government around a shared purpose. In 2024, Ethiopia's parliament allocated between $63 million and $140 million annually to restore degraded land. As the country prepares to host COP32 in November 2027, Kedir has a message for the world: water and trees deserve priority. Most of this transformation, observers note, started the same way—someone deciding to plant something and not stopping.
quick_facts: Ethiopia planted 48 billion trees in seven years through the Green Legacy Initiative
Deforestation rate dropped 70% from 92,000 hectares in 2013 to 27,703 in 2023
Forest cover rose from 15.5% to 23.6% between 2013 and 2023
Halima Kedir in Berbere district walks an hour each way to water her seedlings
Ethiopia will host COP32 climate summit in Addis Ababa in November 2027
